why: Check 1 holds: its PASS/FAIL conditions only compare the CSV and --tsv outputs on stdin, which is what expect line 1 asks for. Check 2 holds: "mentions --tsv and says what it does" fairly reads "documents". Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its heading is "Existing behaviour: npm test passes", and its PASS condition is "exit 0 with no failing tests" and its FAIL condition is "any failure". Neither expect line asks for the test suite to pass, so this is a stricter test that the words don't force. It sits in a real PASS/FAIL check instead of under an Advisory heading, and the verifier brief has no Advisory section at all. Because one check fails the criterion, the output as a whole does not meet it.
